sentences.text: Mullerornis modestus is the sole species within the extinct genus Mullerornis, standing about 1.49 meters tall and weighing approximately 80 kg.
This extinct elephant bird from Madagascar went extinct approximately one millennium ago.
Its eggs were much smaller than those of Aepyornis, weighing about 0.86 kg with a shell thickness of 1.1 mm.
The genus was formally described in 1894 by Alphonse Milne-Edwards and Alfred Grandidier, who named it to honor Georges Muller, a French explorer killed in 1892 by the Sakalava people.
Isotopic evidence indicates that Mullerornis was a browsing herbivore.
Based on optic lobe size, Mullerornis was likely nocturnal but may have also been active during twilight.
Mullerornis is classified in the order Struthioniformes and the family Aepyornithidae.

Mullerornis lived during the Late Pleistocene to Holocene, from 0.129 to 0 million years ago, with radiocarbon dating of a bone suggesting it survived until approximately 1260 years before present, though other estimates place its extinction approximately one millennium ago.
